In cases of a medical emergency, the CLD Provider has primary response authority and provides initial ground medical support to crew and coordinates with the NASA Crew Surgeon as circumstances permit. Once the medical emergency is deemed resolved, medical authority and responsibility for care of the USG crew shifts back to the NASA Crew Surgeon. In cases where the USG crew seek assistance from the CLD Provider for non-urgent medical issues, the CLD Provider Console Medical Team informs the NASA Crew Surgeon, who provides care to the USG crew. The CLD Provider establishes a Console Staffing Plan for all Flight Control Team Operators. A CLD Provider Flight Surgeon is a member of the front room FCT. The CLD Provider provides immediate access to a CLD Provider Flight Surgeon either via physical presence on console or via technological means (i.e., video, voice, etc.) to respond to medical emergencies. The CLD Provider Flight Surgeon is on console to support such contingencies within a reasonable timeframe. NPR 7123.1, National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) Systems Engineering Processes and Requirements defines HSI as: A required interdisciplinary integration of the human as an element of a system to ensure that the human and software/hardware components cooperate, coordinate, and communicate effectively to successfully perform a specific function or mission. Human System Integration domain activities associated with operations, training, human factors engineering, safety, maintainability and supportability, habitability, and environment are considered concurrently and integrated with all other SE design activities. A key tenet of HSI is to implement a human-centered design approach to system development, production, testing, and

ineering, safety, maintainability and supportability, habitability, and environment are considered concurrently and integrated with all other SE design activities. A key tenet of HSI is to implement a human-centered design approach to system development, production, testing, and sustainment. It uses a technical management process and technical disciplines to identify and mitigate risks to programs and projects in cost, schedule, and technical performance. As such, the Human Systems Integration Plan (HSIP) is a key human rating product required in SOMD-CSD-10001, Commercial Low-Earth Orbit Destination System Human Rating Certification Requirements and Standards for NASA Missions. 1.1 PURPOSE The purpose of this document is to describe the HSIP for CLDP Phase 2. During Phase 1, via Space Act Agreements (SAAs), the CLDP’s HSI approach with Commercial LEO Destination (CLD) Partners was through insight and guidance. The HSIP for Phase 2 formally defines the Program processes and organizational roles and responsibilities for planning and executing HSI in order to manage, guide and evaluate Commercial LEO Destination (CLD) Provider’s HSI processes, activities, and products to ensure compliance to CLDP requirements and human rating certification. 1.2 SCOPE This document establ

NASA’s ASCRS, under the supervision of the NASA Crew Surgeon, are responsible for the development and implementation of the exercise prescription for USG crewmembers. The primary goal of the exercise prescription is to optimize muscular strength and function, bone mineral density, and cardiovascular fitness prior to flight. Individual pre-flight physical training plans are developed for each specific mission profile and are customized for each crewmember. Customization considers individual abilities, and the mission objectives assigned to each crewmember. While USG crew are on travel for CLD Provider-conducted training and during the Health Stabilization Program (HSP), the CLD Provider provides access to facilities and resources for USG crew to continue pre-flight exercise and for remote ASCRS support. 5.2.2 MISSION INTEGRATION AND OPERATIONS SUPPORT 5.2.2.1 TIMELINE DEVELOPMENT The CLD Provider leads the pre-flight and in-flight planning and integrated scheduling of all in-flight activities to ensure that such timelines meet ground rules and constraints. Im Bedarfsfall muss eine zusätzliche Lieferung einzelner Sperrelemente innerhalb von 24 Stunden gewährleistet werden. Diese Verpflichtung gilt auch an Wochenenden und gesetzlichen Feiertagen. Zur Bekämpfung von Wettbewerbsbeschränkungen hat der Bieter auf Verlangen Auskünfte darüber zu geben, ob und auf welche Art er wirtschaftlich und rechtlich mit Unternehmen verbunden ist. 3 Angebot 3.1 Das Angebot ist in deutscher Sprache abzufassen. 3.2 Für das Angebot sind die vo n der Vergabestelle vorgegebenen Vor drucke zu verwenden . Das Angebot ist bis zu dem von der Vergabestelle angegebenen Ablauf der Angebotsfrist einzureichen. NPR 7123.1, National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) Systems Engineering Processes and Requirements defines HSI as: A required interdisciplinary integration of the human as an element of a system to ensure that the human and software/hardware components cooperate, coordinate, and communicate effectively to successfully perform a specific function or mission. Human System Integration domain activities associated with operations, training, human factors engineering, safety, maintainability and supportability, habitability, and environment are considered concurrently and integrated with all other SE design activities. A key tenet of HSI is to implement a human-centered design approach to system development, production, testing, and

ineering, safety, maintainability and supportability, habitability, and environment are considered concurrently and integrated with all other SE design activities. A key tenet of HSI is to implement a human-centered design approach to system development, production, testing, and sustainment. It uses a technical management process and technical disciplines to identify and mitigate risks to programs and projects in cost, schedule, and technical performance. As such, the Human Systems Integration Plan (HSIP) is a key human rating product required in SOMD-CSD-10001, Commercial Low-Earth Orbit Destination System Human Rating Certification Requirements and Standards for NASA Missions. 1.1 PURPOSE The purpose of this document is to describe the HSIP for CLDP Phase 2. Die eingesetzten Zufahrtschutzsysteme müssen in ihrer Zertifikation mindestens folgenden Regelwerken entsprechen: • ASTM F2656/2656M • PAS 68:2013 • IWA 14–1 :2013 • DIN SPEC 91414 • DIN SPEC 91414-1 • Technische Richtlinie „Mobile Fahrzeugsperren“ Polizei – SK1B • ISO 22343-1:2023 Die eingesetzten Systeme müssen insbesondere folgende Anforderungen erfüllen: • nachweislich fahrzeugrückhaltend, • geeignet zur temporären Aufstellung, • standsicher und kippsicher, • modular einsetzbar und • kurzfristig auf- und abbaubar. 7 Erreichbarkeit des Auftragnehmers Der Auftragnehmer hat einen Ansprechpartner für die Auftraggeberin zu benennen. Im Bedarfsfall muss eine zusätzliche Lieferung einzelner Sperrelemente innerhalb von 24 Stunden gewährleistet werden. Diese Verpflichtung gilt auch an Wochenenden und gesetzlichen Feiertagen. gangsbreite von mindestens 1,20 m vorzusehen. Die Überfahrhöhe der Konstruktion soll 70 mm nicht überschreiten. Das System muss so konzipiert sein, dass einzelne Sperrsegmente bei Bedarf manuell abgesenkt werden können, um kontrollierte Durchfahrten, beispielsweise für Einsatz - oder Servicefahrzeuge, zu ermöglichen. Zudem muss die Anlage betrieben werden können, ohn e dass eine permanente Aufsicht oder Bewachung erforderlich ist, und eine hohe Widerstandsfähigkeit gegen Vandalismus und Manipulationsversuche aufweisen. Das Produkt muss ganzjährig in mindester 5-facher Ausführung zur Vermietung bereitstehen. Ferner soll es mindestens ISO 22343-1 sowie DIN SPEC 91414-1 zertifiziert sein. -L4- 11.5 Das Produkt soll ein mobiles, geprüftes Zufahrtschutzelement zur temporären Sicherung von Veranstaltungsflächen, Fußgängerzonen und sensiblen Bereichen gegen unbefugtes Befahren durch Kraftfahrzeuge darstellen.
